Open diagonal is 6c O 5d O 4e O 3f, open horizontals on rank 4 are 4c 4d 4e 4f and 4d 4e 4f 4g. No drop gives an immediate four; minimal forced win is two O plies.

Core persistent claims:
* f4 printed = f3 bottom is the canonical triple threat. After O:f4, rank 4 is 4d O 4e O 4f O. O threatens 4c to make 4c 4d 4e 4f, 4g to make 4d 4e 4f 4g and 3f to make 6c 5d 4e 3f. X can block at most one, so O wins on next move.
* c4 printed = c3 bottom is a forcing open three. After O:c4, rank 4 is 4c O 4d O 4e O. The only immediate rank completer is 4f. If X does not take 4f X, O wins at once with 4f O. If X is forced to 4f X, column f opens and O wins next with 3f O on the diagonal 6c O 5d O 4e O 3f O. Forced win in two O plies.

Disagreement on g4 printed = g3 bottom persists:
* Colleagues 1,2,3,5 argue O:g4 makes 4d O 4e O _ 4g O with 4f in the middle of 4d 4e 4f 4g. O threatens 4f O to make 4d O 4e O 4f O 4g O. If X does not take 4f O wins at once on the rank; if X is forced to 4f X column f opens and O wins next on the diagonal 6c O 5d O 4e O 3f O before X can use the d6 e5 f4 g3 threat. They treat g4 as right-hand mirror of c4 and list c4,f4,g4 as three fastest optimal first drops, i.e. c3,f3,g3 bottom-origin with f3 the canonical triple threat.
* Colleagues 4,6 argue g4 does not create a contiguous three-in-a-row on rank 4; 4d O 4e O _ 4g O has a gap at 4f, so O does not create an immediate contiguous open three. 3f is only reachable after column f is filled to 4f by gravity, so the diagonal is not playable after g4 unless X first occupies 4f. Hence g4 is a waiting move / second-move reply to the f4 fork, not an independent optimal first shot. They keep only c4 and f4 as genuine independent first moves that give a guaranteed win in at most two plies, with f4 the classic double/triple threat.

Notation confusion persists between printed top-origin labels used on the board and conventional bottom-origin 1 = bottom labeling: f4 printed = f3 bottom, c4 printed = c3 bottom, g4 printed = g3 bottom.

Unresolved: whether g4 is counted as an independent optimal first move with the same two-ply forcing structure as c4, or only as a reply continuation of the f4 fork. Three-move view c4/f4/g4 vs two-move view c4/f4 split persists, 1,2,3,5 for three moves and 4,6 for two moves. No immediate winning drop exists; minimal forced win remains two O plies under the three-move view.
